short: Age output from tongue ultrasound (M08) is new but unproven: frames of the same children sit in training and validation (M12, behind), so speaker identity can explain the gain.
position: The paper changes one component, the output (M08): a speaker's age regressed by a CNN from single B-mode tongue frames [@xu2021age]. The output is new (none of the 99 paralinguistic studies in the Appendix matches an age-estimation pattern), but the verdict is standard because the evidence does not show that age is decoded. Frames of the same children fall on both sides of a random 80/20 split (§4.1), so a network that recognises the child returns that child's age, and a single ultrasound frame identifies speakers with 3.16% error in [concurrent] work [@shandiz2021neural]. Evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work, which tests held-out children on the same UXTD corpus and finds them well below seen children [@ribeiro2019speaker]. The abstract's "MAE" values are validation MSE in the body, taken on the data used to pick the augmentation (§4.3–4.4), and the proposed speech-therapy use is not tested. The claim that tongue images carry age information beyond speaker identity (§4.4) is unsupported.
